how_this_was_built: Each entry names a funding program a student founder could plausibly find, plus what a correct catalog row about it must contain.

Ground truth is the program's own public page, read by a person or an agent under instruction to quote verbatim. It is NOT derived from data/opportunities.seed.json, from the scraper, or from any code in this repository — a benchmark whose answers come from the system under test measures nothing.

expected_award / expected_deadline record what the page stated at the date given. They are allowed to go stale; when they do, the benchmark reports a mismatch and a human decides whether the page changed or the catalog is wrong.

in_scope=false entries are deliberate negatives: real programs a student-founder catalog should NOT carry, because they are equity investments, tuition scholarships, non-cash, or closed to students. Recall that counts them as hits is measuring the wrong thing.

programs.name: VentureWell E-Team Program
programs.note: The old /e-team-grants/ URL 404s and is the worked example in data/README.md.

programs.name: ScarletPitch
programs.note: Deadline dates on the page carry no year, so a correct row leaves deadline UNKNOWN rather than guessing one.

programs.name: RBS Business Plan Competition
programs.note: $50,000 is the combined pool, not one team's award. Deadline shown is last cycle's.

programs.name: New Business Model Competition
programs.note: Open to any current student of a Northern NJ area college, so a Rutgers founder qualifies.

programs.name: Rohrer New Venture Competition
programs.note: Mixed instrument: the top award is a convertible note, only part of the pool is non-dilutive. A correct row records that rather than calling the whole thing a grant.

programs.name: Thiel Fellowship
programs.note: Above the $2K-$50K band but non-dilutive and student-accessible; a catalog that misses it is missing a real option.

programs.name: Neo Scholars
programs.note: JavaScript-rendered site. A static verifier cannot confirm its quotes, so a correct catalog marks this unverified rather than trusting it.

programs.name: NSF I-Corps Teams
programs.note: Requires NSF lineage and an institutional submission; a student cannot apply alone.

programs.name: Rice Business Plan Competition
programs.note: Requires at least one graduate student on the team, so an all-undergraduate team is not eligible.

programs.name: Hult Prize
programs.note: DELIBERATE NEGATIVE. The Foundation takes equity in the winner, so it fails a non-dilutive founder's hard filter. Finding it is fine; recommending it to an equity_ok=false founder is not.

programs.name: Z Fellows
programs.note: DELIBERATE NEGATIVE. $10,000 arrives as an investment on a $1B valuation cap, not a grant.

programs.name: Rutgers MTC Code for Impact Hackathon
programs.note: DELIBERATE NEGATIVE. Four non-cash prizes. Discovery should find it; funding triage should drop it.

programs.name: Ansary Entrepreneurship Competition
programs.note: DELIBERATE NEGATIVE for a Rutgers founder. Entry runs through Stevens senior-design courses.

programs.name: EPA P3 Student Design Competition
programs.note: DELIBERATE NEGATIVE. The agency's own page says there are no open funding opportunities. A catalog may carry it, but only as unverified or clearly expired.

programs.name: UPitchNJ
programs.note: DELIBERATE NEGATIVE. Reached by winning ScarletPitch, not by applying. Surfacing it as something to apply for is a false lead.
